questions.q: Why does Thomas say there is no shame in ending an unhealthy relationship?
a: Clinging to an outdated ideal can keep you from happiness
Most relationships are doomed from the start
Marriage was never meant to last more than a decade
Separation always leads to a better partner
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the real shame lies in holding onto old ideals that stop you from living the life you should.

questions.q: Why does the promise of staying together until death fit modern couples poorly?
a: Life expectancy was far shorter when the vow began
Divorce was illegal in the fourteenth century
Couples married much later in life back then
The vow originally applied only to royalty
questions.why: The summary notes that when the vow started, lives were about 40 years shorter and marriage was largely economic.

questions.q: What is the core idea behind being kind during a breakup?
a: Your actions toward others shape what returns to you
Kindness makes your ex more likely to come back
It hides your true feelings from friends
It guarantees a faster legal divorce
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes conscious uncoupling as built on karma: kindness plants seeds that blossom in your own life.

questions.q: When does the author say conscious uncoupling is not a good approach?
a: When one partner is abusive
When children are involved
When the couple owns a home together
When the breakup is mutual
questions.why: The summary notes a caveat that the method may not suit victims of an abusive relationship.

questions.q: What does becoming a love alchemist involve?
a: Turning past pain into love and honoring what you gained
Finding a new partner as quickly as possible
Confronting your ex about their faults
Cutting off all contact with your ex permanently
questions.why: Step four asks you to transform contention into love and appreciate what the lost relationship taught you.
